When the client has stopped reading and the queue is full, the push blocks, and `Buffer#abort`, which runs when the client disconnects or a write times out, waits indefinitely for the same monitor. Each such response could permanently hold a web server thread and its `ActionController::Live` thread, possibly resulting in a DoS vulnerability through thread exhaustio

This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. Modern controllers can simulate everything from the recoil of a gun to the resistance of pulling a bowstring — but there's still something missing. No Summary Calling len() on a 0-dimensional tensor under torch.compile previously leaked an internal IndexError during Dynamo tracing instead of matching PyTorch eager's TypeError . This prevented standard try...except TypeError exception handling in user code and caused compilation to fail. Root Cause TensorVariable.sq_length_impl ( torch/_dynamo/variables/tensor.py ) unconditionally traced size(0) . For 0-d tensors, _method_size_stride indexed an empty size tuple, causing an internal IndexError during tracing. Fix Updated TensorVariable.sq_length_impl to check ndim . When ndim is known to be 0 , Dynamo now explicitly raises TypeError("len() of a 0-d tensor") to match eager Tensor.__len__ . If ndim is unknown, existing behavior is preserved. Test Plan Added unit tests to TestTensorLen in test/dynamo/test_len_protocol.py covering len() , __len__ , and Tensor.__len__ on 0-d tensors, try/except handling

The modern version uses an ESP32, a speaker, and salt. The patterns depend on the resonance points of the plate. The device has a rotary encoder to tune different frequencies. Check it out in the video below. There’s also an OLED display to show the frequency and patterns. There is also a 3D-printed enclosure. The patterns, of course, depend on standing waves. We aren’t sure that there’s any practical value for it, but we like the way it looks. This isn’t the first time we’ve talked about Chladni .
